stem.text: The function f is twice differentiable at every x in the closed interval \( [-1, 6] \), with \( f'(0) = 0 \) and \( f''(0) > 0 \). Must f attain an absolute minimum value on the closed interval \( [-1, 6] \)? Justify the answer.

answer_key.label: Yes, because f is differentiable, so continuous, on the closed interval \( [-1, 6] \), so the Extreme Value Theorem applies.

worked_solution.text: The interval \( [-1, 6] \) is closed and bounded.
The function f is differentiable, so continuous, on the closed interval \( [-1, 6] \).
Both hypotheses of the Extreme Value Theorem hold, so f attains an absolute minimum value on \( [-1, 6] \). The theorem gives existence only, not where the value occurs.
